name: John Locke
worldviewSummary: Locke holds that individuals have natural rights to life, liberty and property, that legitimate government rests on consent and exists to protect those rights, and that a government which violates its trust may be resisted. In epistemology he is an empiricist: the mind begins without innate ideas and knowledge derives from experience.
biography: English philosopher and physician associated with the Whig opposition. His Two Treatises of Government and An Essay Concerning Human Understanding were both published in 1689 (dated 1690).

concepts.description: In the state of nature everyone is bound by a law of nature not to harm another in life, health, liberty or possessions.
By mixing one's labour with what is held in common, one makes it one's property, provided enough and as good is left for others and nothing spoils.
The mind at birth is like white paper void of characters; all ideas come from sensation and reflection.

positions.statement: Political power is legitimate only by the consent of the governed, and its end is the preservation of the members' lives, liberties and estates.
When a government acts contrary to the trust placed in it, power reverts to the people, who may establish a new legislature.

The care of souls does not belong to the civil magistrate; belief cannot be compelled by force, so the state should tolerate differing religious worship (though Locke excluded atheists and some others).
Labour creates most of the value of things, and the protection of property is a central purpose of government.

relations.note: Rejects absolute, unlimited sovereignty in favour of limited government (scholarly comparison).
